review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped the neighbouring files (StableElementary, StableDeterminant) for uses of finBlockEquiv and finStabilize_apply. They have no copy of this index-bound argument. The four finStabilize_apply_in*_in* lemmas (lines 50–90) share a `change … simp only [reindexEquiv_apply, Equiv.symm_apply_apply, …]` pattern. That is routine unfolding of a single API lemma, so I did not report it. The map/lift/hom_ext proofs are short wrappers. The only real repetition is the block-index bound inside finStabilize_apply. It sits in one proof rather than across two, and it is only three lines long, so the finding is modest. I did not compile the proposed lemma.

findings.excerpt:
have hcol : n ≤ (finBlockEquiv h (Sum.inr col)).val := by
      rw [finBlockEquiv_inr]
      simp only [Fin.val_cast, Fin.val_natAdd]
      omega
findings.problem: The same index argument is proved four times in this one proof, in the cases inl/inr, inr/inl and twice in inr/inr. It shows that the underlying natural number of `finBlockEquiv h (Sum.inr _)` is at least `n`. The argument is: rewrite with `finBlockEquiv_inr`, simplify `Fin.val_cast` and `Fin.val_natAdd`, then close with `omega`. The statement is identical up to the variable name (`row` or `col`). Each copy also has to be kept in sync with changes to `finBlockEquiv_inr`'s form. The fact is about `finBlockEquiv` itself, not about stabilization, so it belongs next to `finBlockEquiv_inr`.
findings.proposed_change: After `finBlockEquiv_inr` (line 31), add a lemma `theorem le_val_finBlockEquiv_inr {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (i : Fin (m - n)) : n ≤ (finBlockEquiv h (Sum.inr i)).val`. Proof: `rw [finBlockEquiv_inr]; simp only [Fin.val_cast, Fin.val_natAdd]; omega`, which is the existing block verbatim. Then replace the four copies with `have hcol := le_val_finBlockEquiv_inr h col` and `have hrow := le_val_finBlockEquiv_inr h row`. Their hypotheses are unchanged: `h : n ≤ m` and `row col : Fin (m - n)`. The later `simp only [dite_eq_right (not_lt.mpr hrow), …]` calls use these exactly as before. If wanted, a sibling lemma `finBlockEquiv_inl_val_lt` could replace the `Fin.val_castLE` side of the `inl` cases in the same way.
findings.benefit: This removes about 12 duplicated tactic lines and leaves each case of `finStabilize_apply` with only its case-specific simp and exact steps. The lemma is also available to later index-bookkeeping proofs, for example in `finStabilize_comp`, which runs `omega` over similar facts. A change to the `finBlockEquiv` definition then needs one proof update instead of four.

finBlockEquiv h (Sum.inr i) = Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le h) (Fin.natAdd n i)
